name: on-exception — the milestone agent returns early on a skipped gate, and the orchestrator serves the stop
why: A milestone agent cannot ask the user anything, so `on-exception` is the one run mode that has to cross the boundary. The rule is split: the milestone agent returns IMMEDIATELY with outcome stop_requested when it hits a skipped gate or an exhausted bound — so the human sees the trouble before more budget burns — and the orchestrator serves the stop at the boundary, writing paused. Nothing else covers the mode-stop-inside-a-milestone path: strategy-b proves the stops that must NOT fire, verdict-escalation exercises on-exception in the shared tail where no milestone agent exists, and neither one has an agent that had to hand a question back. It also fixes the ledger direction under delegation: the milestone agent PROPOSES a skipped_gates entry and the orchestrator APPENDS it, so the recorded ledger is never smaller than what the milestone agent reported.
